svg.title: An UPDATE writes a new row version and keeps the old one
svg.desc: A PostgreSQL heap drawn as page rectangles: two pages of live tuples at 48 MB, then twelve pages after five rounds of full-table updates, ten of them dead, at 284 MB for the same 200 000 live rows. VACUUM marks the dead pages free but the file stays 284 MB; VACUUM FULL rewrites the heap back down to 47 MB at the cost of an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.
svg.text: An UPDATE writes a new row version and keeps the old one
UPDATE every row x5 -> 284 MB, the same 200 000 live rows plus 999 959 dead
VACUUM -> still 284 MB. The space is reusable; the FILE is not smaller.
VACUUM FULL -> 47 MB, rewritten - but ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, the table is offline
an UPDATE writes a NEW row version and leaves the
old one behind. The row count never changed.
COPY 100 000 rows 295 ms vs the same rows as autocommit INSERTs 83 773 ms (284x)
...so what does autovacuum do while you sleep?
